reviewer_caveat: no shell available to the reviewer; every regex verdict traced by hand and flagged as needing a probe. All were verified by the implementer before being accepted.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: The true-positive set is unchanged; every detector tuple entry still fires from a message.
doubts.disproof_attempt: 'a package.json-only bump' fired touches_build before this change (the old pattern was the wholly unguarded r'package\.json') and fires nothing after it, because the intermediate trailing guard (?![\w-]) rejects the hyphen. The whole taxonomy misses the string, so risk_flags goes from [touches_build] to []: no small floor, no performance_test_layer, and per iteration-reviews.md 'When Self-Review is Sufficient' no full code-reviewer either. The per-entry test cited as proof uses one hand-written template with the name at end-of-string, so it proves each entry fires in one syntactic position, not that the true-positive set is unchanged.
doubts.resolution: Verified before accepting: before=True, now=[]. '-' removed from the trailing class; the guard is (?!\w)(?!\.\w). Hyphen compounds fire again. Accepted cost: package.json-old also fires (over-firing, the preferred direction). Pinned by test_a_build_input_in_a_hyphen_compound_still_fires. Mutation Q1 caught by 30 tests, previously 0.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: The narrowing is safe because the diff surface already refuses these strings.
doubts.disproof_attempt: Not true for every newly-refused string, and the method conflates the two things the change exists to separate. touches_build_files never receives prose tokens, it receives git diff paths. For 'package.json-only' the file being named is package.json, and the diff of such a change contains package.json, on which the diff surface returns True — so the surfaces disagree on the same real change, newly, in the unsafe direction. The diff also resolves the identical ambiguity three different ways: trailing '.' gets prose semantics, trailing '-' gets literal semantics, bare config stem gets literal semantics.
doubts.resolution: Same root as the finding above; fixed by the same one-character change. The '.' and '-' cases are now decided by one stated rule: a following character either continues the name or extends it, or else it is prose.

doubts.disproof_attempt: Every cited test exists and executes what it is cited for, and every param count is right. But the trailing-hyphen decision was taken by this diff and had no test and no ledger row, while the two other declined-narrowing decisions each got both. It is also invisible to the mutation evidence: mutating (?![\w-]) to (?!\w) fails ZERO behavioural tests, only the string-comparison guard.
doubts.resolution: The decision itself changed, and is now pinned behaviourally (29 params x 2). Ledger row 15 added; mutation Q1 added to round 4 and caught by 30 tests.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: self-review.json now describes the shipped implementation (Stage-1 finding 6 closed).
doubts.disproof_attempt: It certifies the pre-Stage-2 implementation. Arithmetic: '157 cases' against the shipped 164 — exactly the two tests Stage 2 added; 'the new test file 282' where the split produced two files; risk_taxonomy.py 248 where the shipped file is 257; two mutation rounds where three were run; no mention of the non-capturing group. reviews.json corroborates by timestamp: self completed 10:04:27, code 10:21:24, never re-recorded.
doubts.resolution: Root cause is ordering, not arithmetic: the self-review was recorded before later stages changed the code, so it went stale twice. It is now regenerated LAST, after every code change, with every number re-measured from the tree.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: The observable classification outcome is unchanged for the five config families.
doubts.disproof_attempt: touches_build enforces ['performance_test_layer']; touches_middleware enforces ['mandatory_review']. The flags go from [touches_middleware, touches_build] to [touches_middleware], so the enforces union loses performance_test_layer and the recorded risk_flags list changes. The test whose docstring asserts this checks only flag membership, not the property it claims.
doubts.resolution: Claim corrected in the spec, the Stage-2 disposition and the test docstring. The test now asserts the enforcement difference explicitly rather than implying it away.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: The shipped review record is an accurate ledger of the review that happened.
doubts.disproof_attempt: reviews.json records the spec gate as findings_count 0, although Stage 1 rejected twice and raised 7 findings across three rounds. The 'only blocking findings are recorded' reading fails, because the code row records all five of its findings including three non-blocking lows.
doubts.resolution: The round-3 citations are now carried in the spec-review payload's spec_citations and the row re-recorded, so findings_count reflects the review that happened.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: All 21 JS entries disagreed before; 0 disagree now.
doubts.disproof_attempt: The 21 is right, but 'disagree' is measured over different populations in the two halves (tuple entries vs 15 hand-written probes), and unqualified '0 now' is false: the trailing-punctuation relaxation creates eight new literal-token divergences (pyproject.toml. fires from a message, touches_build_files returns False), which under the old symmetric guard had AGREED. The residue paragraph lists the next.config.foo and case residues but not this one.
doubts.resolution: Both populations are now named in Root Cause and the punctuation divergence is listed with its rationale (a diff never contains a path ending in a sentence period).

doubts.claim_under_doubt: The trailing guard rejects a further extension but allows sentence punctuation.
doubts.disproof_attempt: Traced by hand through every backtracking path: package.json.bak, next.config.js.bak, webpack.config.js.orig, pipfile.locked, requirements.txt.bak, requirements-dev.txt.bak, setup.python, setup.pyc, package.json5 all correctly refused; comma, semicolon, question mark, paren, backtick, quote, slash, backslash, newline and a sentence-final period all correctly allowed. Only pathological cases behave oddly (package.json..bak fires).

summary: 8 doubts, 7 REFUTED (2 high, 3 medium, 2 low), 1 SURVIVES. The load-bearing one is a single root: the trailing guard rejected '-' unconditionally, so a real dependency-change message lost its flag entirely — and the Stage-2 disposition that closed it without a code change was itself refuted. All seven refutations were verified empirically by the implementer (the reviewer had no shell) and fixed.
